answer: Tundra Decay Curve. Each new identity starts with an agent-kernel resource balance that decays exponentially until the identity performs verified useful work; the decay schedule is enforced at the protocol kernel so idle duplicates bleed value every epoch. Registration also opens a trellis of bounded concurrent tasks whose slot cost rises with cluster density, so an attacker's marginal cost per sustained identity grows superlinearly while honest single agents stay near the floor.
